requirement_text: IELTS Academic — Level 1: Overall score of 6.5 and a minimum of 6.0 in each component.
limitations: UCL assigns each programme one of five levels; the level that applies is stated on the individual programme page, not here. This record states what Level 1 requires, not which programmes need it.
researcher_notes: UCL publishes five English levels. Each level is recorded as its own row with the level in `scope`, because a student needs the specific level their programme demands, and collapsing five different thresholds into one row would show the wrong number to most applicants.

requirement_text: "CAE, CPE, IELTS, TOEFL, and Trinity test scores must be achieved from one sitting. We will not accept individual components scores from multiple tests."
researcher_notes: A rule that disqualifies a superscored result. Recorded because a student who meets every component across two sittings does not meet LSE's requirement, and the score rows alone would not tell them that.

requirement_text: IELTS Academic — Higher level: "7.0 overall (minimum 6.5 in all elements)". Imperial College London considers IELTS scores to be valid for 2 years.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT — Standard level: "92 overall (minimum 20 in all elements)"; Higher level: "100 overall (minimum 22 in all elements)". Under the scale introduced on 21 January 2026 the equivalents are "4.5 (minimum 4.5 in all elements)" for standard and "5.0 (minimum 5.0 in all elements)" for higher. "Tests taken before 21 January 2026 will be accepted according to the old requirement as long as they are taken within the two-years of the start date."
limitations: Two different TOEFL scales are live at once; which one applies depends on the date the test was sat.
researcher_notes: Kept as one row deliberately: splitting the old and new TOEFL scales into separate rows would let a student read one scale's number and miss that it only applies to tests sat before or after 21 January 2026.
test_scale: TOEFL iBT — both the 0-120 total scale and the banded scale introduced 21 January 2026

requirement_text: IELTS: 7.5 overall, minimum 7.0 per component. Oxford recommends the IELTS Academic option; "The IELTS General, IELTS UKVI General and IELTS Life Skills options are not suitable for admission; we are not able to accept IELTS Online."
researcher_notes: Read from the page's own accepted-qualifications table after expanding the collapsed section (the table is not present in the page's collapsed text). The page states one set of scores; it does not split standard and higher levels, and the words "standard level"/"higher level" do not appear on it.

requirement_text: TOEFL iBT: 110 overall, with minimum component scores Listening 22, Reading 24, Speaking 25, Writing 24. "TOEFL tests taken up to and including 20 January 2026 are accepted." "NB. TOEFL tests taken from 21 January 2026 are not accepted and do not meet the English language condition. Changes to the TOEFL iBT test were introduced on 21 January 2026 and are currently under review by the University."
limitations: Oxford states it is still reviewing the post-21-January-2026 TOEFL, so this exclusion may change.
researcher_notes: High-impact for a student choosing which English test to sit: Oxford currently accepts no TOEFL taken from 21 January 2026 onwards, while UCL, Imperial, KCL and Warwick all publish scores against the new scale. A student who sits TOEFL now has no Oxford-valid result.
test_scale: TOEFL iBT total 0-120 with section scores

requirement_text: Other accepted English qualifications and scores: C1 Advanced 191 overall, minimum 185 per component; C2 Proficiency 191 overall, minimum 185 per component; Pearson PTE Academic 76 overall, "Minimum 66 in Speaking, Listening, Reading and Writing. We do not require particular scores in the Enabling Skills."; Oxford Test of English (Advanced) 165, minimum 155 per component.
limitations: Pearson PTE Academic Online is no longer accepted per the same table.
researcher_notes: Recorded because with TOEFL currently excluded these are the practical alternatives to IELTS for an applicant from Turkey.
test_scale: Mixed scales — Cambridge English Scale, PTE 10-90, Oxford Test of English 0-140 per section

requirement_text: "If you are offered a place, you will need to show the correct level of proficiency by 31 July in the year you receive your offer."

"If you are studying for the Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitime Diplomasi / Anadolu Lisesi, you are strongly recommended to undertake further study if you wish to apply to Cambridge. Applicants with Devlet Lise Diplomasi / Lise Bitime Diplomasi / Anadolu Lisesi alone will not be competitive and are unlikely to be successful." Suitable alternatives listed include A Levels, the International Baccalaureate, 5+ AP Tests at Score 5 with an overall grade of at least 85, or completion of the first year of an undergraduate degree outside the UK.
researcher_notes: The single most decision-changing requirement found for a Turkish applicant in this pass: Cambridge states in its own words that the Turkish national high school diploma alone is not competitive, and names the qualifications that are. A student planning on the Turkish diploma route needs this before choosing a curriculum, not after applying.

requirement_text: "Each course and programme we offer has its own requirements in terms of English test scores." The University publishes typical ranges rather than one threshold: IELTS overall scores from 5.5 to 7.5+, and TOEFL iBT from 72 to 109-120, and directs applicants to the individual course profile for the score that actually applies.
limitations: Manchester publishes NO university-wide English threshold. The ranges quoted here are the page's own illustrative examples and must not be read as a requirement a student can meet — the binding number is on the course page.
researcher_notes: A real negative result recorded rather than skipped: unlike UCL, KCL, Warwick and Imperial, Manchester does not band centrally at all. Recording the absence is the honest answer to "what English score do I need for Manchester?" — the answer is that only the course page can say.

requirement_text: "Acceptable English language tests (such as IELTS, TOEFL, Pearson and Trinity ISE etc) are deemed to be valid for two years after the test date, and must be valid on the start date of the course."
researcher_notes: Manchester's validity rule is university-wide even though its score thresholds are not, so this one IS answerable centrally.

researcher_notes: Worth flagging for anyone re-verifying this row: a web search summary of the same page reported Band A as IELTS 6.5. The page itself says 6.0. The page won.

requirement_text: Tests must be "completed in one sitting" and taken "on or after 1 September 2024 for September 2026 entry only"; tests must fall within "two years and one month prior to the start of your course". "IELTS 'One skill Retake' not acceptable".
